## Service Tab

The Service tab is used for configuring the source for SCADA Request if gas quality data is missing. The SCADA Request service (FcSrvAutoRescan.exe) will look for missing data within the time frame configured on the Service tab. If data is missing, information about the missing data will be written to the SCADA Request table in the database so that the SCADA system can read and attempt to rescan the data.

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Data Field Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available on the Service tab:

- **Rescan Data** - When set to "Yes", the SCADA Request service is enabled for the source.

  The Auto Rescan service (FcSrvAutoRescan.exe) must be installed and running.

- **Log Rescan in Exceptions Log** - When set to ‘Yes’, an exception will be generated when data is missing, and a request has been written to the database for the SCADA system to rescan the data.

- **Rescan Frequency** - Determines if the service should rescan at an hourly or daily frequency.

- **Time Elapsed Before Considered for Rescan** - Amount of time (days or hours) the service waits until it rescans for missing data. Valid values are 0 to 30 (for days) and 0 to 23 (for hours).

  Data is considered missing if it is older than the values entered.

- **Number of Prior Days Considered** - The time frame for which the service processes data. Specifies the number of days prior to the current date that the service will scan for missing data. Valid values are 1 to 60. For example: If you enter 60, the service will not examine data that is more than 60 days old.

- **Daily Rescan Hour** - When Rescan Frequency is set to Daily, this value determines what time of the day to process data.
